intro: You are on the bank of the Tunca, at Edirne Palace in Edirne province, from 1450–1475. Before Topkapı, this was the Ottomans' principal palace. It was destroyed when its magazine was blown up in 1878, and today its foundations are slowly being excavated.
history: Begun under Murad II and finished under Mehmed II, the palace on the bank of the Tunca was the Ottomans' principal seat before Topkapı. Picture a wide compound: the Cihannüma pavilion, baths, kitchens and hunting lodges. So how did it vanish? In 1878, during the Russian occupation, its magazine was blown up and most of the palace came down. Now excavation is bringing its foundations back to light.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the foundations of the Cihannüma and the Kum Kasrı bath, then the remains of the kitchens and the Justice pavilion.
facts: Did you know? The palace was the headquarters for Ottoman campaigns in Europe, and sultans went on residing here long after İstanbul was taken. Begun before Topkapı, it was one of the principal palaces of the Ottoman sultans. Most of it came down in 1878, when its magazine was blown up during the Russian occupation.
outro: This brings our journey through Edirne Palace to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These foundations are still telling their story; let them keep telling it to those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
